subject: wizardBookshelf
pitch:
Category: Prop group.
Subject: wizard's bookshelf with tomes, scrolls, orbs and candles.
Style: high-fantasy anime.
reasoning:
I need to plan each edit as precise SEARCH/REPLACE blocks with exact line matches. The camera framing is controlled by the app rather than our module, so I can't directly fix the cut-off moon at the top—but I can adjust element bounds or sizes within our control to influence how the auto-framing behaves.

Now moving to the actual edits, starting with the hero grimoire layout. I'm replacing the single book row with two narrower upright books flanking the orb, working out how their width and rotation (yaw/roll tilts) affect their footprint so they don't collide with neighboring elements.

Working through the rotation math to position the book correctly — figuring out how roll about z and yaw about y combine to determine the lowest touching corner against the base.

I'm checking whether the leaning book's top corner clears the neighboring narrow book's edge at x=-0.29, accounting for both roll and yaw offsets, and it looks like -0.302 stays clear with a small margin before I factor in the yaw-adjusted front corner position.

Continuing the rotation math, the book's corners span roughly x=-0.558 to -0.302 after applying the tilt, so I'm checking whether this overlaps the left narrow book positioned near -0.585, keeping within the shelf's ±0.6 inner bounds.

Checking the thickness extents confirms the gaps clear by about 5mm on both sides, so I adjust the depth placement, moving the display book's z-center forward to around 0.11 to sit closer to the shelf front while accounting for the yaw rotation about y.

Writing helper function for positioning...

Now I'm laying out the book's structure: front and back covers as thin boxes offset along the depth axis, with a slightly recessed page block inset from the edges to suggest visible pages beneath the covers.

I'm designing the front cover decoration with a wine-colored texture featuring a gold double-border, corner flourishes, a central rune ring, and an eight-point star emblem, plus working out a separate extruded gilt clasp shape for the closure.

Scaling the crescent outline down to fit as a plaque, then setting up the extrusion axes aligned to the book's local orientation...

For the book clasp I'll use the same rotation trick with x as local up and y as negative local right, so thickness still extrudes toward the front. I'm adding a small glowing gem at the crescent's center, keeping it subtle so the gold clasp stays the dominant element, and picking a deep wine tone for the cover texture.

For the cover artwork itself, I'm using a transparent-background texture with alpha cutout so the cover color shows through except where the gold border lines, rune ring, star, corner brackets, and bottom flourishes are drawn, placed slightly above the cover surface and sized to the front panel's aspect ratio. I'll skip texturing the spine since it faces away from view, and the page block's fore-edge will only be visible at an angle through the recessed gap.

Now I'm adding four gilt corner pieces positioned near each corner of the front/back panels, boosted in brightness, plus setting the main cover color. I'll inline the decoration code directly into the compartment-5 replacement rather than defining a separate helper function, and I need to make sure the brighter gilt constant is defined using the existing metal palette function.

I'm refining the metal tones: keeping the bright version as the primary gilt, and defining a darker "aged" variant using a bronze metal with reduced tarnish for secondary elements like studs and balls.

I need to replace all the old gilt/gold references across the shelf strip, uprights, carcass trim, cornice studs, and corners with these new AGED and AGED_C variants, being careful each search target matches a unique location since there are many edits to make across the module.

For the wood, I'm lightening the violet grain tones by 20-25% into a muted plum-brown palette, adjusting the WOOD_V, WOOD_H, RAIL, and WOOD_D color pairs to reduce contrast while keeping the hue family.

I also want the side panel rails slightly lighter than their recessed centers, keep the crest's wood fill mostly as-is, and reduce contrast in the front uprights' vertical grain striping. For small bevels on boxes, I'm thinking of adding a helper that extrudes a rectangular outline with a slight bevel along the depth axis instead of using sharp-edged boxes.

Defining the bevel helper...

Right, since the extrude is along z with the outline in the xy plane, the bevel rounds the front-facing rim edges of the cornice (the large z-facing plane), giving a nice chamfer along the front.

The top and bottom edges stay plain, which satisfies the "3-5mm bevel to prominent edges" requirement, and the rectangular 4-corner outline accepts the bevel fine without needing corner smoothing. For the side panels I'm lightening the frame rails and inner box, and doing the same for the back boards and backing wood, though I should check whether the back is actually visible behind the mural plane.

For the back-facing boxes, which read dark since their normals point away from the light, I want to soften the shading function so the darkening and highlight tints are more muted plum-brown tones rather than the current harsh dark purple and violet values.

I'm introducing a muted color palette for book covers alongside the bright ones, weighting thin books toward muted tones and tomes toward brighter covers, though I need to be careful since drawing from the RNG stream in a different order will shift the deterministic layout downstream.

Adjusting color distribution for brightness...

Swapping gilt and brass fixture colors for aged tones...

Continuing to adjust color constants across the cornice trim, studs, and lying corner elements, swapping various GOLD/GILT references to AGED or AGED_C where appropriate.

Now I'm moving to gems and ribbon decoration on tomes, keeping those as-is, before turning to the orb texture mapping. For orbs, I need to rework the sphere UV coordinates so the front hemisphere gradient is centered correctly around u=0.25 instead of the current symmetric doubled-gradient approach.

Writing new orb texture SVG...

Writing swirl paths and core highlight...

Writing SVG gradients...

Adjusting the cyan tint parameters for the cup and shelf highlights, tuning the radius and blend amounts near the top surfaces.

Lowering both violet orb strengths to 0.8 while keeping gold core at 1.0. I'm also considering a glowing pool disc under the blue orb, but a radial gradient plane would hard-cut with alphaTest, so I'll rely on the existing paint tint instead.

For the moss on the platform, I want to shift from random noise-based patches to three fixed moss centers at specific points, and I'm adjusting the platform step dimensions—lower step 1.7×0.86 and upper step 1.8×0.94 with two height levels.

Still writing platform shader logic...

Darkening the rug colors and toning down the crystal glow, making the crystal color more muted and reducing its brightness strength before touching the glow/lathe call that renders the crystal shape.

For the scroll's rolled ends, I want to add a visible spiral pattern on the exposed paper faces rather than just the plain cap rings, distinguishing it from a wax seal look. I'll texture the end caps with a parchment-colored disc featuring a dark spiral path, positioned at the cylinder's end faces alongside the existing gold cap.

I'm sizing the gold knob smaller so the spiral pattern remains visible around it, since the current radius would fully cover the center face -- shrinking it to about r*0.3 should let the spiral show through.

For the texture, I'm generating an SVG with a parchment-colored circular background and computing a spiral path by stepping through angles from 0 to 6π, increasing radius proportionally as it winds outward.

Now I'm thinking through the ribbon detail—currently there's a torus ring around the scroll plus a cylindrical wax seal, but I want to make the knot more distinct by adding a proper ribbon bow.

I'll add a small knot ball on top of the ribbon with two tilted tail boxes, and reposition the wax seal to a separate spot so it's clearly distinguishable from the ribbon's bow shape.

Adjusting the seal position and adding spiral end-cap circles to the scroll edges...

For the hourglass vessel, I'm thinking about how to get a translucent glass look—maybe using a cloned material with transparency, though that risks being lost when the harness merges parts into one mesh on export. An alternative could be faking it with an alpha-cutout texture instead of true transparency, but mapping that onto a lathe shape adds complexity I need to weigh.

I'm worried that if opacity settings get lost, the glass shell would turn opaque and hide the sand entirely, so I'm looking for a more robust approach — maybe building the hourglass silhouette out of thin ring sweeps at various heights instead of a solid enclosing shell, so the sand stays visible regardless of material fallbacks.

I'll skip the shell approach and settle on 8 meridian ribs plus a few rings per bulb to suggest a lattice glass vessel, since true transparency risks looking opaque. Now I need to define the radius profile along the height for each bulb, marking where the widest point sits for the rings to align correctly.

Now I'm positioning the brass plates against the glass bounds, then shaping the sand masses as lathed heaps—a cone-like pile settling at the bottom bulb and an inverted mirror shape forming the upper mass.

Still refining the sand mound profile coordinates...

Now I'm adding a thin sand-colored rod as a stream element connecting the lower sand peak to the upper sand surface, using a small cylinder with a soft glow effect.

I need to replace the entire hourglass function body, keeping the signature unchanged, so I'm carefully reconstructing the original lathe profile and cylinder caps to match exactly for the edit.

Checking that each search block I pick is unique in the file before applying the edits.

I confirm the texture-selection line is unique and plan to change the threshold from 0.4 to 0.75 so muted spines use fancy texture more often, while verifying existing plain and gold label colors still read fine against muted covers. I'm also looking for where to add a MUTED color constant near the COVERS array.

Adjusting the wood grain lines and the lit function's shading mix to use the new palette constants, noting this will subtly lighten the dark wood variant too.

I'll settle on plum-brown tones like "#40303b" and "#463540" for V/H, with RAIL slightly lighter at "#4a3944"/"#513f4a".

Now I'm adding a bevel helper function right before the cylinder helper definition, inserting it ahead of that existing line.

Writing extrude call for bevel...

Still adjusting beveled trim placements...

I should also double-check the camera framing against the crescent moon's height, since the tallest extent might be the crescent crown rather than the candle flames, and I don't want the render to cut it off.

The perspective crop at the top is something I can't fix, so I'll just note it honestly and move on to the grimoire object for compartment 5, setting up its dimensions, tilt angles, and position before building a rotation helper for placing its corners in 3D space.

Building grimoire cover geometry...

Adding cover texture plane and gilt corner accents...

I want the moon clasp positioned slightly toward the bottom-center so it sits in front of the texture's central emblem, hiding it from view. I'm designing the texture itself with a border, corner flourishes, and a central rune ring with an 8-point star, sized so the crescent moon clasp naturally covers that star when placed in front.

Working out the crescent's geometry now, it ends up bowl-shaped like a U with the opening facing upward, leaving a gap where the star peeks through underneath. I'm thinking of placing a small glowing cyan gem right in that opening, at the star's center, as a focal highlight.

Writing texture SVG...

Still building the sigil defs...

I'm reconsidering how to safely replace the old function without triggering unused variable errors, deciding it's simpler to just carefully copy the exact text verbatim rather than trying clever renaming tricks.

Writing SVG gradient code...

Working through the sphere's lighting geometry, I'm mapping the radial gradient coordinates to the front-view projection so the core highlight, midtone, and rim shading align correctly with the texture's equator and poles.

Still writing gradient defs...

I'm now confirming the seams align properly across the duplicated halves, and checking that the armillary sphere and book textures use the right gilt tones. I'm starting to list out all the search-and-replace edits needed, ordered by importance, making sure none of the target text overlaps with earlier edits.

For the first edit, I'm positioning two narrow upright books near the hero's left side, computing their coordinates so the front faces line up correctly within the shelf.

I'm adjusting the hero book's depth placement to align its front face with the narrow books, settling on gz=0.12 so the fronts match at roughly 0.1475. I'm also checking the parameter naming for rotation and texture in the box/plane geometry helpers used in the grimoire scene.

Now I'm working out the clasp geometry, scaling a crescent outline down by 0.4 and extruding it along the gilt metal with specific bone attachment and bevel settings for the book's latch detail.

Writing tick marks for the hero texture...

Still writing SVG star and rune details...

Now adding new palette constants for aged brass tones and muted candle colors, then adding an aged metal variant alongside brass for variation.

Adding the uprights and shelf strip, then starting on the cornice piece...

Updating more edits...

Adjusting orb placements and checking the platform edge-noise logic for the weathering effect.

Now I'm defining the rug tile pattern with alternating dark maroon colors and the stone scale texture, then moving to the scroll geometry with torus ribs positioned along its length.

Still refining the scroll knot and tail details...

Adding the spiral discs facing inward with the parchment texture, then layering a gold knob over the spiral center, and starting the hourglass element code with its glass color definition.

Writing the hourglass sweep profile...

Now I'm setting the sand color to a warm gold, tinting the glass pale, and leaving the brass posts loop untouched. I'm checking the catmull import and planning a small edit to soften the dark shading mix on the hourglass vessel surface.

Adjusting the wood and rail color constants so the rail reads lighter than the central wood tones, keeping their declaration order intact, and adding a bevel helper alongside the cylinder utility function.

For the plaque, I'm inserting the HERO and SPIRAL elements right before the existing PLAQUE definition, confirming that string appears exactly once in the file. I still need to verify the grimoire's box/glow build logic, the DEG constant, and the placeBook counts before writing out the final summarized answer.

critic.text:
1. **Replace the blank teal wedge in the upper-left bay with a clearly presented hero grimoire.** The bookshelf already reads instantly; this is the best opportunity to give its “face” a distinctive focal detail. Replace the leaning end of `row(-0.59, -0.24, BT[4], ...)` with a dedicated display book: approximately **0.22 m wide × 0.27 m tall × 0.055 m thick**, centered near `x = -0.43`, with its broad cover facing forward. Use about **−12° yaw and −8° roll**, and calculate its height so the lowest cover corner touches `BT[4]`. Add a recessed page block, four substantial gilt corners, and one large moon or star clasp; retain two narrow upright books beside it. **The next render should show an unmistakable decorated grimoire, not a broad, undecorated triangular shape.**

2. **Give the crown safe framing in every view.** The back render cuts into the moon-and-orb silhouette at the top, and the header crowds it. Adjust the render camera target and orthographic scale or distance to leave **roughly 5–7% clear margin above the highest flame or crescent**, with the complete platform still visible below. Keep the three-quarter view as the primary presentation; do not shrink the model to accommodate distant sparkles. **The next four views should contain the entire prop, with no crown detail touching an image edge or label.**

3. **Separate the cabinet’s structural surfaces from its nearly black recesses.** The side and back currently collapse into a dark purple slab, while the front’s wood grain produces conspicuous vertical striping. Lighten `WOOD_V`, `WOOD_H`, and `RAIL` by roughly **20–25%**, using muted plum-brown rather than stronger violet; retain `WOOD_D` for shelf recesses and inset panels. Reduce each `grain()` color pair’s contrast, and give the recessed side-panel frames a slightly lighter edge than their centers. Add only a **3–5 mm bevel** to prominent cornice, plinth, and upright edges. **The next render should reveal cabinet thickness, joinery, and framed panels without losing the dark, enchanted interior.**

4. **Establish a quieter color hierarchy instead of giving every book and border equal emphasis.** In `placeBook()` and `row()`, make roughly **two-thirds of the thin books** muted indigo, aubergine, worn wine, or desaturated teal, with `SP.plain` or restrained bands. Reserve brighter covers, large spine symbols, gems, and bright gilt for the larger tomes and the new display book. Split `GILT` usage into darker aged brass for secondary shelf strips, straps, and corner fittings, and brighter gold for the crest and principal magical objects. **The next front view should read as grouped libraries of books, with a few treasured volumes—not a wall of equally bright symbols and yellow lines.**

5. **Make the orbs look internally magical rather than like solid colored beads.** Keep the blue orb as the strongest interior light source. Rework `orbTex()` so its cloud and swirl remain visible on the front hemisphere, with a darker lower rim, an off-center luminous core, and one controlled pale highlight. Reduce the detached white highlight sphere in `orb()` to approximately **half its current apparent area**. Strengthen the localized cyan tint on its cup and nearby shelf top, but do not wash the entire bay blue. Keep the violet orbs dimmer. **The next render should show contained luminous depth and a small pool of reflected color, while preserving the orb’s round silhouette.** The deliberately floating magical stars can remain floating.

6. **Quiet the platform so it supports the bookshelf instead of competing with it.** The saturated green marks in `PLAT` read as a checker-like decorative pattern rather than incidental moss. Remove most of them, keeping a few muted patches at **two or three outer stone joints**, and reduce the contrast of the `STONE` pattern. Darken the rug’s checker variation while retaining its clean border; slightly mute the cyan floor crystals so they do not outshine the blue orb. **The next three-quarter render should lead upward from the floor props into the shelves, rather than repeatedly pulling attention to the platform perimeter.**

7. **Give the small storytelling props stronger identifying features, not more scattered ornament.** In `scrollLying()`, add a visible dark spiral or concentric inset to the exposed parchment ends and make the ribbon knot distinct from the wax seal. In `hourglass()`, replace the single opaque yellow lathe with a pale, low-opacity or subtly tinted vessel containing **two separate sand masses and a narrow central stream**; keep the brass supports clearly outside it. **The next close view should distinguish rolled parchment from capped rods and an hourglass from a solid gold ornament, while the full view remains clean.**
